definition: Maps pixels or video frames into a latent representation.
pitfall: A condition projector may resemble an encoder but need not model a posterior.

definition: Maps latent representations back to pixels or frames.
pitfall: A denoising decoder may also perform a diffusion step, as in LTX-Video.

definition: An encoder-bottleneck-decoder system defining the tokens consumed by a generative model.
pitfall: Tokens may be continuous tensors or discrete indices.

definition: A probabilistic autoencoder with a regularized latent distribution.
pitfall: Modern 'VAE' implementations may use perceptual and adversarial objectives beyond the original ELBO.

definition: Maps continuous encoder outputs to discrete codebook entries.
pitfall: Codebook collapse and inactive entries can reduce effective capacity.

definition: Feature dimension at each latent spatial-temporal position.
pitfall: More channels improve reconstruction but make the DiT prediction problem harder.

definition: Ratio from H,W pixels to latent H/f,W/f.
pitfall: It is distinct from DiT patch size and from total token compression.

definition: Output at time t does not depend on future frames.
pitfall: A nominal causal convolution can still break streaming if normalization or padding uses future context.

definition: Feature-space distance, commonly LPIPS, used to preserve perceptual detail.
pitfall: It can trade pixel fidelity for plausible texture and must be balanced with reconstruction losses.

definition: Discriminator-based objective encouraging realistic local statistics.
pitfall: Starting too early or weighting too highly can destabilize reconstruction.

definition: Precompute or freeze tokenizer outputs while training the DiT.
pitfall: No gradient improves decoder defects; tokenizer quality is a hard ceiling.

definition: Decoder that consumes latent plus an auxiliary observation such as LR frames.
pitfall: It can recover details from the observation but may over-copy degradations without robust training pairs.
